comparison: Both address viral tracing and anatomical claims (C29-C37). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with adequate quantification (n=6 mice, 129 cells, 274 axons, statistical analysis), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating the experiment 'lacks adequate quantification' and that claims about hippocampal collaterals and VGAT immunoreactivity are 'anecdotal.' Major disagreement on sufficiency of quantification.

Both address molecular marker characterization (C38-C43). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by quantitative immunohistochemical data (62 neurons, 6 mice), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting better explanation of what SATB1 immunoreactivity indicates and which cell groups correspond to previously identified populations. Disagreement on clarity and interpretation of molecular markers.

Both address electrophysiological recordings and theta/gamma coupling (C44-C49). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical testing and sample size (n=8), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to lack of transparency about total recordings, selection criteria, and how the 8 labeled neurons were chosen. Disagreement on methodological transparency and potential selection bias.

Both address anatomical and immunohistochemical characterization (C50-C54). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by juxtacellular labeling data (8/8 PV+, 6/6 SATB1+, etc.), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning selection criteria and whether the proportion of labeled neurons matches viral tracing expectations. Overlap with concerns about sampling methodology.

Both address anatomical projections to EC (C55-C58). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by detailed anatomical data, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning what happened to the 3/8 neurons without EC collaterals and raising concerns about selective reporting. Disagreement on completeness of anatomical reporting.

Both address target selectivity and synaptic connections (C59-C64). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by electron microscopy and quantification (11/11 boutons forming synapses), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to small sample size (13 targets from 1 cell) and requesting clarification on number of mice used. Disagreement on adequacy of sample size for target selectivity claims.

Both address behavioral state classification (C65-C68). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with clear methodology, and peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, noting no concerns were raised about these methods. Strong agreement on behavioral state classification methodology.

Both address firing patterns across behavioral states (C69-C73). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by quantitative analysis (n=8 cells), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, finding descriptions unclear and questioning what specific terms mean. Disagreement on clarity of presentation rather than data quality.

Both address identification of putative orchid cells (C74-C77). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by firing criteria and validation, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning false positive/negative rates when criteria are applied to all neurons. Disagreement on reliability of classification criteria.

Both address control experiments and comparison to Teevra cells (C78-C80). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by negative controls and statistical comparison, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, finding descriptions unclear about which cells are referenced. Disagreement on clarity of reporting.

Both address simultaneous LFP recordings from CA1d and EC (C81-C86). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by appropriate statistical testing (n=4 mice), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, finding experiments 'quite confusing,' questioning whether data came from only 1 mouse and the novelty of findings. Disagreement on clarity and scientific contribution.

Both address stereological counting data (C87-C91). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by quantification from 3 mice with low error coefficients, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting better comparison to cell labeling data and normalization to total populations. Disagreement on how well stereological data connects to functional characterization.
OpenEval evaluated background/contextual claims (C1-C2, C9-C28) as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluated discussion/interpretation claims (C93-C102) as UNCERTAIN, noting mix of well-supported conclusions and speculative interpretations requiring validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluated mechanistic hypotheses (C103-C113) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are appropriately identified as speculative but require experimental testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these speculative mechanism claims.

OpenEval evaluated functional interpretation claims (C114-C121) as SUPPORTED, combining solid anatomical observations with reasonable inferences, though some speculation requires validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these functional interpretation claims.

Peer reviewers raised concerns about claim C3 (not extensively evaluated by OpenEval in isolation), which appears to be part of the viral tracing methodology. This concern is captured in the R2/R1 pairing but C3 specifically was not a focus of OpenEval's grouped evaluation.
